title: Exact additive extension by zero adjoint to localized restriction
statement: For a sheaf of rings R on a Grothendieck site and an object U, assuming the localized restriction functor preserves zero morphisms, there is a functor G from localized R-module sheaves to R-module sheaves preserving finite limits and finite colimits, together with an adjunction G ⊣ restriction, and the localized restriction functor is additive.

proof.text: Construct the presheaf extension by direct sums over arrows V → U, then apply module sheafification. Maps from each summand to F(V) identify naturally with maps into restriction, yielding the adjunction. A monomorphism induces an injection on every summand and therefore on their direct sum. Module sheafification has underlying abelian sheafification, which preserves monomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. Thus G preserves monomorphisms; being an additive left adjoint, it is right exact, hence exact and preserves finite limits and finite colimits. Restriction preserves addition sectionwise.

lean.statement:
theorem localized_restriction_adjunction
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{max u v}) (U : C)
    (hzero : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{max u v} R U).PreservesZeroMorphisms) :
    ∃ (G : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (R.over U) ⥤ SheafOfModules.{max u v} R),
      PreservesFiniteLimits G ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits G ∧
      (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{max u v} R U).Additive ∧
      Nonempty (G ⊣ SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{max u v} R U)
